sentences.text:
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 551 of 2023
Applicant :- Promod Kumar Singh And

Another
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. Deptt. Of Home And Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Anup Kumar Mishra

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Shree Prakash Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, Sri B.N. Nishad, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The instant application has been filed with a prayer to quash the entire criminal proceedings of the Case Crime No. 587 of 2019 in Criminal Case No. 5550 of 2021, under sections 406/420 I.P.C.
relating to Police Station-Kotwali City, District-Pratapgarh, pending in the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Pratapgarh and impugned Chargesheet dated 17-12-2020 and summoning order dated 24-03-2021 issued by the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Pratapgarh.
Learned counsel appearing for the applicants submits that the applicants are innocent and have falsely been implicated in the instant case.

He next added that the dispute pertains to a registered sale deed wherein the allegation against the applicants is that they have taken the amount of sale consideration in their accounts though he submits that the fact is otherwise, and the role of the present applicants are only to the extent that they have got recognized the vendee with the vendor and nothing else and thereafter, due to enmity, the instant F.I.R.has been lodged against the present applicants and applicants are suffering for their no fault.

He next added that a civil suit for recovery Promod Kumar Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. ... on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98780127/
1 of the sale consideration is also pending and the matter pertains to a civil dispute which is being given colour of criminality.

entities.text: Promod Kumar Singh And Another vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He next added that the criminal proceedings initiated against the applicants may be quashed.

On the other hand, learned A.G.A. appearing for the State has opposed the contention aforesaid and submits that there are specific allegations against the present applicants and the applicants have taken amount in their accounts and thus, there are sufficient evidences against them and thus, they are not entitled for any relief.

After the argument at length, learned counsel for the applicants submits that interest of justice would be sub-served, if this Court directs the court below to permit the applicants to appear before the court below and file an application of discharge.
He further submits that the court below may be directed to decide the discharge application within stipulated period of time, as may be fixed by this Court.
Learned AGA for the State has no objection to the aforesaid submission.

In view of aforesaid, the applicants are permitted to file an application for discharge before the court below within a period of 15 days from today through their counsel and if such an application is filed,
the same shall be decided within a further period of 30 days, strictly in accordance with law.
With the aforesaid observation, the application is disposed off.
